answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake bonded to a single verifiable task history: an agent must lock a small bond and complete costly, checkable work before its votes count, so creating many identities multiplies the cost instead of the influence. Think of each honest agent as an island that earns trust slowly, like bees returning with nectar after repeated trips, while a sable-coated newcomer with no history starts with zero weight until its work is attested by independent peers.
